knowledge_point.title: Integrating Products Containing Trigonometric Functions Using Substitution

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u=5 x^{2} - \frac{\pi}{4}$. Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=10 x.
$$

Change both bounds:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\sqrt{\frac{\pi}{10}}&\Longrightarrow u=\frac{\pi}{4}\\x=\sqrt{\frac{7 \pi}{60}}&\Longrightarrow u=\frac{\pi}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting, including the required constant factor, gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int_{\sqrt{\frac{\pi}{10}}}^{\sqrt{\frac{7 \pi}{60}}} 5 x \sin{\left(5 x^{2} - \frac{\pi}{4} \right)}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\frac{1}{2}\left(\int_{\frac{\pi}{4}}^{\frac{\pi}{3}} \sin{\left(u \right)}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Integrate and evaluate at both bounds:

$$
\left[- \frac{\cos{\left(u \right)}}{2}\right]_{\frac{\pi}{4}}^{\frac{\pi}{3}}=\left(- \frac{1}{4}\right)-\left(- \frac{\sqrt{2}}{4}\right).
$$

Simplifying gives

$$
- \frac{1}{4} + \frac{\sqrt{2}}{4}.
$$

$$
- \frac{5 \sqrt{3}}{16} + \frac{5 \sqrt{2}}{16}.

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\sqrt{\frac{\pi}{6}}&\Longrightarrow u=\frac{\pi}{6}\\x=\sqrt{\frac{5 \pi}{24}}&\Longrightarrow u=\frac{\pi}{4}\end{aligned}

Substituting, including the required constant factor, gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int_{\sqrt{\frac{\pi}{6}}}^{\sqrt{\frac{5 \pi}{24}}} - 3 x \cot{\left(2 x^{2} - \frac{\pi}{6} \right)} \csc{\left(2 x^{2} - \frac{\pi}{6} \right)}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=- \frac{3}{4}\left(\int_{\frac{\pi}{6}}^{\frac{\pi}{4}} \cot{\left(u \right)} \csc{\left(u \right)}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}

$$
\left[\frac{3 \csc{\left(u \right)}}{4}\right]_{\frac{\pi}{6}}^{\frac{\pi}{4}}=\left(\frac{3 \sqrt{2}}{4}\right)-\left(\frac{3}{2}\right).
$$

Simplifying gives

$$
- \frac{3}{2} + \frac{3 \sqrt{2}}{4}.
$$
